tasks.description:

phases.name: Core data pipeline
phases.description: Implement git log parsing and commit categorization/enrichment — the pure data transformation functions.

tasks.title: Implement parseGitLog in git.ts
tasks.description:
Implement the `parseGitLog` pure function in `src/git.ts`. This function takes a raw git log string and returns `Commit[]`.

Parsing strategy:
1. Split the raw string on `---COMMIT---` separator.
2. For each non-empty block, extract fields:
   - Line 1: full 40-char SHA
   - Line 2: subject (first line of commit message)
   - Lines 3 through `---BODY_END---` marker: body (may be empty, may contain newlines)
   - Line after `---BODY_END---`: author name
   - Next line: author date in ISO format with offset (e.g., `2026-03-30 10:00:00 +0000`)
   - Remaining lines before next separator: `--stat` output
3. Parse `--stat` output: individual file lines match pattern `path | N +++---` and summary line matches `N files changed, N insertions(+), N deletions(-)`.
4. Build `FileStat[]` from individual file lines, extract total insertions/deletions from summary.
5. Construct `Commit` object with `timestamp` as a `Date` from the author date string.
6. If a block is malformed (missing SHA, subject, or author), throw an Error identifying the malformed block.
7. Empty input returns empty array.

Also implement `readGitLog` which uses `spawnSync` to call git log with the format string, `--no-merges`, date range filters, and `--stat`. Throw appropriate errors per spec FM-3 and FM-4.

Keep the COMMIT_SEPARATOR and GIT_FORMAT as module-level constants.
acceptanceCriteria: parseGitLog with three-commit fixture returns array of 3 Commit objects
Each Commit has correct sha, subject, body, author, timestamp, filesChanged, insertions, deletions
parseGitLog with empty string returns []
parseGitLog with malformed block throws with identifying message
readGitLog throws 'git is not available on PATH' when spawnSync result.error is set
readGitLog throws with repo path and stderr when git exits non-zero

tasks.title: Implement categorize.ts functions
tasks.description:
Implement all functions in `src/categorize.ts`:

**categorizeCommit(commit: Commit): CategorizedCommit**
- Strip leading whitespace from subject
- Match lowercased subject against regex `^(feat|fix|refactor|docs|chore|test|style|perf|build|ci)(\(.+\))?:`
- Use matched prefix as CommitCategory, or 'other' if no match
- Call extractTilItems and assignDaySegment to populate derived fields
- Return CategorizedCommit with all original Commit fields plus category, tilItems, daySegment

**extractTilItems(subject: string, body: string): string[]**
- Scan subject and body for lines containing `TIL:` (case-sensitive)
- Extract text after `TIL:` to end of line, trimmed
- Return array of extracted strings (may be empty, may have multiple)

**assignDaySegment(timestamp: Date, tzOffset: string): DaySegment**
- Parse the timezone offset string (e.g., '+0530', '-0800') to compute the local hour
- The timestamp Date object represents the absolute time; use the offset to derive the local hour
- Map hour to DaySegment: 05-11 → morning, 12-16 → afternoon, 17-23 → evening, 0-4 → night

**buildRepoEntry(repoPath: string, commits: Commit[]): RepoEntry**
- Categorize each commit via categorizeCommit
- Sort by timestamp ascending
- Extract repoName as basename of repoPath
- Return RepoEntry

**buildDiaryEntry(date: string, repos: RepoEntry[]): DiaryEntry**
- Collect all TilItems from all repos, preserving repo order then commit timestamp order
- Deduplicate by exact text match, keeping first occurrence
- Build TilItem objects with text, repoName, and short SHA (7 chars)
- Return DiaryEntry

Note: assignDaySegment needs the original timezone offset string from the git timestamp, not the Date object alone. The categorizeCommit function will need to receive or derive this offset. Consider storing the raw timestamp string on Commit or passing it separately.
acceptanceCriteria: categorizeCommit assigns correct category for all conventional prefixes
categorizeCommit assigns 'other' for unrecognized prefixes
Prefix matching is case-insensitive
extractTilItems extracts TIL from subject and body
extractTilItems returns empty array when no TIL present
assignDaySegment maps boundary hours correctly per spec
buildDiaryEntry deduplicates TIL items by text

phases.name: Markdown generation and file I/O
phases.description: Implement markdown rendering, existing entry detection/replacement, and filesystem operations.

tasks.title: Implement markdown.ts functions
tasks.description:
Implement all functions in `src/markdown.ts`:

**formatDiaryEntry(entry: DiaryEntry): string**
Generate markdown per spec §8 BR-8:
- Open with `## YYYY-MM-DD`
- If tilItems is non-empty, add `### Today I Learned` section with items formatted as `- Item text (\`abc1234\`, repo-name)`
- For each repo in entry.repos (in order), add `### repo-name` heading
- Under each repo, list commits flat sorted ascending by timestamp: `` - `<7-char-sha>` <subject> — <category> (+<insertions> / -<deletions>) ``
- End with `---` separator
- If all repos have zero commits, return empty string

**findExistingEntry(content: string, date: string): boolean**
- Scan content for a line matching `## YYYY-MM-DD` (the date heading)
- Return true if found, false otherwise

**replaceEntry(content: string, date: string, newEntry: string): string**
- Find the line matching `## YYYY-MM-DD`
- Remove everything from that line through the line before the next `## ` heading (or end of file)
- Insert newEntry at the same location
- Preserve all other content

**appendEntry(content: string | null, date: string, newEntry: string): string**
- If content is null, create new file with top-level heading `# Code Diary — YYYY-MM` (derived from date) followed by newEntry
- If content exists, append newEntry to end of file

All functions are pure — no filesystem access, no subprocess calls.

phases.name: CLI wiring and integration
phases.description: Implement CLI argument parsing, validation, orchestration, replace prompt, and the entry point. Wire everything together.

tasks.title: Implement cli.ts argument parsing and validation
tasks.description:
Implement the full `cli.ts` module:

**parseArgs(argv: string[]): CliArgs**
- Strip first two elements (node + script path)
- Collect positional args as repoPaths
- Parse `--date` and `--output` named flags
- If no repoPaths, write usage to stderr and exit(2)
- Default date to today via `new Date().toLocaleDateString('en-CA')` (YYYY-MM-DD)
- Validate date format with regex `^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$` and check it's a valid calendar date (parse and verify components). If invalid, stderr message and exit(2)
- Default outputDir to `process.cwd()`

**validateRepoPaths(paths: string[]): void**
- For each path, resolve to absolute
- Check `existsSync(abs)` — if not, stderr `Error: path "<path>" does not exist.` and exit(2)
- Check `existsSync(join(abs, '.git'))` — if not, stderr `Error: "<path>" is not a git repository (no .git found).` and exit(2)
- Fail fast on first bad path

**isValidDate(dateStr: string): boolean** (helper)
- Match regex, parse year/month/day, verify month 1-12, day valid for month/year

**promptReplace(date: string): Promise<boolean>**
- Use `readline.createInterface` from Node.js stdlib
- Ask `An entry for YYYY-MM-DD already exists. Replace it? [y/N] `
- Return true only if answer is 'y' or 'Y'

**run(argv: string[]): Promise<void>**
- Parse args, resolve paths, validate
- For each repo: readGitLog → parseGitLog → buildRepoEntry
- Filter out repos with zero commits
- If no commits across all repos, print message and return (exit 0)
- buildDiaryEntry, formatDiaryEntry
- Compute output path: `join(resolve(outputDir), 'diary', `${date.slice(0,7)}.md`)`
- Check for existing entry; handle replace prompt per spec §2 and FM-8
- Write file via replaceEntry or appendEntry
- Print confirmation to stdout

Import all dependencies from other modules using `.js` extensions.
acceptanceCriteria: parseArgs extracts repoPaths, date, outputDir correctly
Missing repos prints usage and exits 2
Invalid date format exits 2 with correct error message
validateRepoPaths exits 2 for non-existent path with correct message
validateRepoPaths exits 2 for non-git directory with correct message
run orchestrates full pipeline: git → categorize → markdown → file
Replace prompt uses readline and respects TTY detection
Non-interactive stdin exits 1 without prompting
Confirmation message printed to stdout on success
src/index.ts calls run with catch handler exiting 2

tasks.title: Write tests for cli.ts parseArgs
tasks.description:
Create `src/__tests__/cli.test.ts` with unit tests for `parseArgs` and `isValidDate`.

Test cases:

**parseArgs:**
- `['node', 'script', '/path/to/repo']` → repoPaths `['/path/to/repo']`, date is today, outputDir is cwd
- `['node', 'script', '/repo1', '/repo2', '--date', '2026-03-30', '--output', '/tmp/out']` → all fields populated
- `['node', 'script']` (no repos) → should call process.exit(2). Mock process.exit and verify.
- `['node', 'script', '/repo', '--date', 'bad-date']` → should call process.exit(2)
- `['node', 'script', '/repo', '--date', '2026-13-01']` → should call process.exit(2) (invalid month)
- Flags can appear in any order relative to positional args

**isValidDate (if exported, or test through parseArgs):**
- '2026-03-30' → valid
- '2026-02-29' → invalid (2026 is not a leap year)
- '2024-02-29' → valid (2024 is a leap year)
- 'not-a-date' → invalid

Mock `process.exit` using `vi.spyOn` to prevent actual exit. Mock `process.stderr.write` to capture error messages.

Missing repos triggers exit 2
Invalid date format triggers exit 2
Invalid calendar date triggers exit 2
process.exit and stderr.write are mocked appropriately

tasks.title: Build and verify end-to-end
tasks.description:
Run the full build and verification process:

1. Run `npm run typecheck` — verify zero errors
2. Run `npm run test` — verify all test files pass
3. Run `npm run build` — verify `dist/` is produced with all expected files
4. Verify `dist/index.js` has shebang `#!/usr/bin/env node`
5. Review architectural constraints from spec §8:
   - `cli.ts` contains no business logic beyond argument parsing and orchestration
   - `git.ts` contains no markdown generation
   - `markdown.ts` contains no filesystem access and no subprocess calls
   - `fileIO.ts` contains no git logic and no markdown generation
   - No module imports from `cli.ts`
   - Zero external packages in dependencies
6. Verify all modules use named exports only, .js extensions in imports, and strict TypeScript
